provider: Scaleway Apple silicon (Bare Metal) - Mac mini M2 'M2-M' (Apple M2, CPU 8C / GPU 10C / Neural 16C, 16 GB unified RAM, 1x256 GB SSD, 1 Gbps)
region_dc: PAR-1 (Paris, France); the pricing page lists PAR-1 as the only availability zone for Apple silicon
sovereignty_class: Full EU sovereignty on corporate/DC side: Scaleway (Iliad group) is French HQ + French DC, so no US CLOUD Act exposure at provider level. Certifications [uncertain]: Scaleway publishes ISO 27001 and HDS for parts of its cloud; whether the Apple silicon product is in scope of these certs is not confirmed. No SecNumCloud and no BSI C5 for this product. Caveat: hardware and macOS licence are Apple (US) but the data stays on a dedicated bare-metal host in Paris.
monthly_cost: EUR 115/month ex-VAT (list price; EUR 0.17/hour). 24/7 per hour = 0.17 x 730 h = ~EUR 124/month, so monthly cap price EUR 115 applies. With 23% Polish VAT ~EUR 141 (B2B reverse charge may apply). Mac mini M2 Pro 16GB is EUR 139/month, M4-S 16GB EUR 149/month. POC-hours: EUR 0.17/h, minimum charge 24 h = ~EUR 4.08 per POC run; 1 week POC ~EUR 28.6. Optional Private Network EUR 9.99/month. Corrects the operator's assumed EUR 70 figure: current price is EUR 115. Fits the <=EUR 150 budget.
billing_granularity: Per-hour billing with a monthly cap; no scale-to-zero: you pay for as long as the machine is assigned to your account and must explicitly delete it. Minimum lease is 24 hours (Apple licensing); deletion only possible after 24 h (auto-delete after 24 h can be enabled). No minimum for Asahi Linux installs.
setup_fee_and_lockin: No setup fee found. Lock-in is only the 24 h minimum lease on macOS (none for Asahi Linux). Exit cost: delete the server, local disk data is lost (back up to Object Storage with restic). Free credit promo (EUR 100 for new Business accounts) seen on a signup page [uncertain, may be outdated].
gen_tps_7b_q4: [uncertain] Not measured by us on this host. Bandwidth-derived: M2 base has 100 GB/s memory bandwidth; Bielik-7B Q4_K_M is ~4.5 GB, so ceiling ~22 t/s, realistic ~14-20 t/s with Metal. Public llama.cpp Apple-silicon benchmark (Llama-7B Q4_0, M2 10-core GPU) reports roughly 20-22 t/s decode, recalled from memory and not re-verified. Note: Scaleway macOS runs on bare metal so Metal GPU is available (no VM passthrough).
prefill_tps: [uncertain] Bandwidth-derived/third-party, not measured on this host. Public llama.cpp benchmark for Llama-7B Q4_0 on M2 10-core GPU shows ~150-180 t/s prompt processing (pp512), recalled from memory. Operator estimate of 50-100 t/s is plausibly a conservative figure for long prompts with Q4_K_M and macOS overhead. Planning range: 80-170 t/s. Compute-bound (10 GPU cores, ~3.6 TFLOPS FP32), much slower than any L4/L40S class GPU.
ttft_at_4k: [uncertain] ~25-50 s at 4k prompt tokens with prefill 80-160 t/s (4000/160 = 25 s, 4000/80 = 50 s). With 8k tool-schema prompts ~50-100 s. Prompt/prefix caching (llama.cpp --cache-reuse, slot prompt cache) is therefore essential for agentic use: only the first request pays this cost.
concurrency_slots: Practically 1-2 slots (-np 2). Decode is memory-bandwidth bound, so extra slots split the ~100 GB/s and prefill compute. KV cache for Mistral-7B-based Bielik (32 layers, 8 KV heads, 128 dim) in fp16 ~0.125 GB per 1k tokens [inference from architecture, uncertain]; q8_0 KV halves that.
ctx_ram_headroom: 16 GB unified RAM; macOS and services take ~3-4 GB, and Metal GPU working set is capped by default at roughly 2/3 of RAM (~10.7 GB, adjustable via iogpu.wired_limit_mb sysctl if permitted [uncertain on a managed MDM host]). Model 4.5 GB + KV: 32k ctx = ~4 GB fp16 fits, so 16-32k ctx is sensible; 64k (~8 GB) is too tight. Recommended: 16-32k ctx, 1-2 slots.
availability_status: Available on demand from the console/CLI in PAR-1 (listed on pricing page with hourly price) [uncertain: real-time stock not verified, Scaleway Apple silicon has occasionally been out of stock]. No waitlist indicated.
egress_traffic: 1 Gbps public bandwidth listed on the product line; no per-GB egress charge or traffic cap was found on the pricing page for Apple silicon [uncertain, not explicitly stated]. Private Network add-on: EUR 9.99/month (1 Gbps) or EUR 19.99/month (10 Gbps), unlimited traffic. One IPv4 per machine plus an IPv6 /128.
electricity_metering: Not applicable: electricity is included in the rental price (it is not colocation). For reference Mac mini M2 draws roughly 5-15 W idle and ~30-40 W under load [uncertain].
hosting_model: Self-hosted bare-metal macOS (or Asahi Linux, but Asahi has no Metal/GPU acceleration for llama.cpp, so macOS is needed). You install llama.cpp (llama-server, Metal build) yourself and control chat template, --jinja and tool-call parser fully. Limits: no physical access, no macOS recovery, SIP cannot be disabled, FileVault impractical; SSH and VNC access; MacPorts, Xcode preinstalled; Homebrew installable. Run llama-server under launchd.
tool_calling_support: Yes, same as any llama.cpp host: llama-server with --jinja exposes OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions with tools and a server-side tool-call parser, as long as Bielik's chat template supports tools [uncertain: Bielik template tool-call quality not tested here]. You control the template, so fixes can be applied.
spec_decode_support: Yes in principle: llama-server supports -md/--model-draft speculative decoding with a draft GGUF, and you own the process. But the M2 is bandwidth/compute-limited with 16 GB, so a second draft model competes for RAM and bandwidth; gain is uncertain. DFlash draft compatibility with llama.cpp on Metal not verified [uncertain].
sla_uptime: [uncertain] No GPU-grade SLA found for Apple silicon; Scaleway Bare Metal products generally publish a SLA in their general terms but the specific figure for Apple silicon was not confirmed. Treat as best-effort, single machine, single zone (PAR-1), no redundancy.
llm_inference_tos: No explicit prohibition on LLM inference found in the FAQ/docs; Scaleway markets M4 Pro Mac mini 'for AI and machine learning' workloads. Apple licensing restrictions (24 h minimum lease) relate to macOS. [uncertain: full Scaleway Service Agreement / acceptable-use policy not read in full]
price_stability: Historically Scaleway Apple silicon prices rose (the operator's reported +45% increase; M2 now EUR 115/month versus the operator's remembered EUR 70) [uncertain on exact history]. Current list: M1 EUR 75, M2 EUR 115, M2 Pro EUR 139, M4-S EUR 149. Hourly billing means you can leave on 24 h notice, which limits price risk.
model_lock_in: None: self-hosted GGUF, so Bielik stays available as long as you keep the file (unlike Scaleway Generative APIs / OVH AI Endpoints catalogs where Bielik was removed). Portable to any other llama.cpp host. Only the minimal setup (llama.cpp build, launchd unit) needs redoing.
